report.summary: All surviving findings are needs-evidence; plan is to resolve them with targeted inspections before any fix.
risks: Several findings depend on code not visible in the provided chunks; inspections may confirm or refute them.
Some paths are unknown; we must locate the actual files before changing code.
Fixes may be unnecessary if inspections show the claims are false.
todos: Run the settling checks listed in the work items to resolve each finding.
After inspections, implement the smallest fixes for confirmed issues.
Add regression tests for any confirmed invariants.

work.what_breaks: Unparsable halves are included in the mutation total, contradicting the comment that they are not counted, skewing the denominator.
work.path: UNKNOWN (file containing lines 568-574, likely in a mutation analysis module)
work.smallest_fix: Inspect lines 568-574; if row['n'] is not decremented for unparsable halves, adjust the logic to exclude them from the denominator.
work.check: Inspect lines 568-574 to see if row['n'] is later decremented for unparsable halves.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if the code is actually correct, the fix could introduce a bug in counting.

work.what_breaks: Role check is case-sensitive, contradicting the docstring's case-insensitive claim, potentially rejecting valid roles.
work.smallest_fix: Change the exact string compare to a case-insensitive comparison (e.g., role.lower() == 'focus').
work.check: sed -n '95,105p' daedalus/focus.py; grep -n 'role' daedalus/focus.py; run existing tests for focus.py.
work.cost_if_wrong: Low: small change, likely matches the documented intent.

work.what_breaks: Independence is defined inconsistently (agreement rate vs. model family vs. weights), leading to ambiguous classification.
work.smallest_fix: Unify the definition by introducing a single shared function that defines independence, and update all references to use it.
work.check: grep -n 'independence' daedalus/council.py daedalus/vendor.py | grep -v '#' and inspect each definition.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: refactoring may affect multiple modules; need to ensure consistency.

work.what_breaks: Multiple modules declare fail-closed policies without a central guard; each must be individually verified, risking drift.
work.smallest_fix: Introduce a central guard module that enforces fail-closed policies, and refactor each module to use it.
work.check: grep -n 'fail-closed\|EXPLICIT-ONLY\|never silently' daedalus/*.py and inspect each module's guard code.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: centralizing could be overkill if each module already enforces correctly; but reduces drift risk.

work.what_breaks: Cross-module invariants (e.g., gate precedence) are not enforced locally at the point of use, risking silent breakage.
work.smallest_fix: Add local assertions or tests at the point of use for each cross-module invariant, or extract them into a shared validator.
work.check: Pick one claim (e.g., gate precedence) and write a test that changes the referenced module's behavior and see if the claim breaks without a local test catching it.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: may require adding tests and possibly refactoring.

work.what_breaks: If multiple adapters implement their own ask methods without a shared reply builder, the contract may break (withheld paths omitted).
work.smallest_fix: Inspect each adapter's ask method; if they do not share a reply builder, refactor to use a shared builder that always includes withheld paths.
work.check: grep -n 'def ask' -A 10 daedalus/adapters/*.py and check each for '_withheld_paths' in the reply construction.
work.cost_if_wrong: Low: if a shared builder already exists, no change needed.

work.what_breaks: The provider may not enforce the egress policy, allowing data to be sent without classification.
work.path: UNKNOWN (provider module, likely daedalus/providers/deepseek.py or similar)
work.smallest_fix: Inspect the provider's run method to confirm it passes the policy to classify_data and enforces the result; if not, add the enforcement.
work.check: Inspect the provider's run method to see if it passes the policy to classify_data and enforces the result.
work.cost_if_wrong: High: if the policy is not enforced, sensitive data could leak.

work.what_breaks: Digest verification may not be universally applied, leaving some artifacts with stale or corrupted data undetected.
work.path: UNKNOWN (artifact writer and digest verification code)
work.smallest_fix: Inspect the artifact writer and digest verification code; ensure all artifacts are hashed and verified.
work.check: Inspect the artifact writer and digest verification code to see which artifacts are hashed and which are not.
work.cost_if_wrong: High: if some artifacts are not verified, corruption may go unnoticed.

work.what_breaks: The rmdir drain and chmod calls may lack fresh verification, leading to TOCTOU vulnerabilities.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect _remove_tree_no_follow; if lstat calls are missing before rmdir and chmod, add them.
work.check: Open _remove_tree_no_follow in the source and search for lstat calls before rmdir and chmod operations.
work.cost_if_wrong: High: TOCTOU could be exploited.

work.what_breaks: Some modules may lack retry logic for atomic publish, risking corruption on platforms where replace is not atomic.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect each module's publish/persist method for retry logic; if missing, add retry logic similar to atomic.py.
work.check: grep -n 'os.replace\|os.rename\|shutil.move' daedalus/providers/*.py daedalus/loop.py and compare against atomic.py's retry implementation.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if other modules use a shared helper, no change needed.

work.what_breaks: The receipt may carry more than the rule label, leaking meta or identity fields.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect the refused turn receipt function; if it does not strip meta and identity fields, add stripping.
work.check: Open the refused turn receipt function and inspect whether it strips meta and identity fields.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if it already strips, no change needed.

work.what_breaks: Liveness quality exit codes may be misclassified, leading to incorrect exit statuses.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect for a shared severity classifier; if none, trace exit-code setting in each checker and unify.
work.check: Grep for a shared severity classifier (e.g., 'classify_liveness' or 'is_quality') across all checker modules and trace exit-code setting.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: may require refactoring checkers.

work.what_breaks: Docstrings asserting contracts may not match implementation, risking drift.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect each module's implementation for a shared base class or validator that enforces the contract; if none, add tests to enforce behavior.
work.check: Inspect each module's implementation for a shared base class or validator that enforces the contract; if none, compare behavior across modules with a test.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: may require adding tests.

work.what_breaks: The module may have write operations not visible in the chunk, but the claim is untestable without the full file.
work.smallest_fix: Open the full module file and grep for write operations to verify the claim.
work.check: Open the full module file (e.g., 'cat daedalus/module.py') and grep for write operations (open, write, os.replace, etc.).
work.cost_if_wrong: Low: inspection only.

work.what_breaks: current_trace_id may never mint a trace, leaving FanoutResult.trace_id always None.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect current_trace_id implementation; if it never returns a non-None trace, fix it to mint when appropriate.
work.check: Open the file containing current_trace_id and verify it returns None when no trace is in scope; also test FanoutResult with and without a trace.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if it works, no change needed.

work.what_breaks: Lanes may skip baseline checks, violating the policy.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect the check runner to ensure all lanes are forced to call baseline checks; if not, add enforcement.
work.check: Inspect the check runner to see if all lanes are forced to call the baseline checks; test a lane that attempts to skip the baseline.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if already enforced, no change needed.

work.what_breaks: The council may have ambiguous output contracts, leading to miscommunication between modules.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect both modules to see if they are the same council or if the gate is downstream; clarify the output contract.
work.check: Inspect both modules to see if they are the same council or if the gate is downstream; check the council's output contract.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: may require documentation or refactoring.

work.what_breaks: Probe nonces may be generated per run instead of per probe and lane, causing collisions.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect probe.py to see how new_nonce is called; if it is not per probe and per lane, fix the call sites.
work.check: Inspect probe.py to see how new_nonce is called; verify it is called per probe and per lane, not per run.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if already correct, no change needed.

work.what_breaks: Secret floor rule may not be called independently, allowing permissive policies to bypass it.
work.smallest_fix: Inspect deepseek.py to see if it calls secret_floor_rule; if not, add the call.
work.check: Inspect deepseek.py to see if it calls secret_floor_rule, and run a permissive policy test on .env files.
work.cost_if_wrong: High: security bypass.

work.what_breaks: Duplicated guards without shared helpers may drift.
work.smallest_fix: Search for secret_floor_rule, transcript append, and worktree walker implementations; if they are duplicated, extract shared helpers.
work.check: Search for secret_floor_rule, transcript append, and worktree walker implementations to see if they are shared.
work.cost_if_wrong: Medium: if already shared, no change needed.

work.smallest_fix: Locate the Selection class and inventory module implementations and check whether they enumerate every field/layer.
work.check: Locate the Selection class and inventory module implementations and check whether they enumerate every field/layer.
